newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR SOFT ON U.S. UNIT AHEAD OF WEEKEND.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR SOFT ON U.S. UNIT AHEAD OF WEEKEND.

text.p: The Zimbabwe dollar weakened against most major currencies on Friday as dealers sought to safeguard their positions ahead of the weekend.
The local unit fell as far as 10.9900/11.000 versus the dollar at one stage before the central bank stepped in to help pull it up, dealers said.
They added that the Zimbabwe dollar was likely to continue to shrink against the U.S. unit next week due to import pressure.

"It moved up as far as 10.9900/11.0000 and it could have been because the market was short, but more than likely dealers were just trying to protect their positions ahead of the weekend," one dealer said.
"The central bank came in at this level and through intervention helped it up a bit. Apart from that, not much happened," he added.
At Friday's close, the Zimbabwe dollar was quoted at 10.9700/9800 on the U.S. dollar from 10.9650/9750 on Thursday. It also softened against the rand to 2.4700/4900 from 2.4515/4555.
But against sterling it inched firmer to 17.8800/9000 from 17.9800/18.0100 previously and against the mark to 6.5900/6.6100 from 6.6400/6500.
Looking ahead to next week one dealer said, "Market sentiment is such that the Zimbabwe dollar will continue to depreciate due to import pressure."
